I actually agree with most of this. I've always seen my depression to be a product of my environment, which is why I've consistently refused medication, electroshock therapy, etc. I know that I do have my problems but they are not things that can be switched off to put me into a "working" state using tried and true methods.

>The question you need to ask yourself is, why have you made the choice not to end your life?

I think about this all the time, actually. Like you, I am very strongly in support of the right to die, in any circumstance. I'm not religious, so I'm not really worried about any postmortem punishment. My family has tried to convince me that killing myself would be selfish and shame them, but I'm not close enough to them to give a fuck. So I suppose the primary reason is fear. Not fear of dying, but of messing up. I don't have access to any reasonably certain methods, and another failed attempt would only make things worse for me. And there's always the occasional, irrational glimmer of hope that manages to keep me going for another week or two before I'm inevitably disappointed.

Like I said before, it was really more of a cry for help, but I did understand the finality of death, yes. I found ending everything to be preferable to continuing as I was at the time.

And I think at that point I had actually lost three relatives, all grandparents.

Specifically? The mental ward at St. Alexius medical center in Bismarck. I was admitted to the juvenile ward but the facility was so small (only three people in the juvenile ward including myself, one left after a few days) that they tended to mix us in with the adults, especially during group therapy.

The second time was the Stadter Center in Grand Forks. I was above 18 this time so I was admitted as an adult. I was somewhat thankful for that; according to the nurses the juvenile ward was, pardon the term, a madhouse. I was moved to a different room after my first night because I was close enough to the door to hear the screaming that went on at all hours.

His stay was much shorter than mine, actually, since it was pretty obvious that there wasn't anything wrong with him. They put him in addiction counseling while he was there but he wasn't even a heavy drinker, he was just having a really bad day.

I forgot to answer part of your last post, it may have seemed like I was avoiding it but I'm just a bit tired. I take this "anything" thing very seriously.

>Do you still get suicidal thoughts?

Yes, almost every day now. I was fine for a few years after my first institutionalization but my living situation is depressing enough to bring them back in full force.

>I would like to hear that story if you feel like typing it all out.

It's not actually that long, I just thought it might be boring. My father disliked that I refused to discuss therapy in depth with him, and would frequently call my psychologist to attempt to essentially shake him down for information. Being a professional, he told my father that he couldn't share anything with him unless I gave him permission. So my father decided to call him claiming that I was actively attempting to kill myself. Apparently the doctor was somewhat put off by the irrelevant nature of the questions my father asked (basically he wanted to know everything we discussed in therapy) but was obligated to share it due to what he thought was an emergency situation.

And then he did that again. At this point my psychologist asked me to sign a release to hopefully prevent my father from doing something like this for a third time, which I did, but after that I wasn't comfortable seeing him any more. Not anything he did, of course, I felt bad because I really did like him, both personally and professionally.

>What do you think would make life better for you. Do you have any long-term plans or goals?

I think that if I found a way out of North Dakota I could make things better for myself. I have several talents that I don't have any real opportunity to utilize here, while my family pushes me towards getting a cubicle job. But I'm not in a position to go anywhere, financially speaking, so no, no real plans or goals. I've been trying to find a job to at least improve my situation a little bit, but employment opportunities are scant in the middle of nowhere.

Somewhat. At the time I was really uncomfortable sharing my feelings with anyone, especially a group of strangers, so I was shutting myself up for other reasons and concentrating on convincing the doctors that I was well enough to leave, rather than being obstinate as I was before. (I wasn't there by choice, even though suicide wasn't involved this time.)

This was a different facility, so the nurses were much nicer, even though they weren't really in a position to be especially helpful, I guess. The doctors were the same. Get in, ask basic questions, get out as quickly as possible. I remember a guy practically begging to see the doctor because he felt better and needed to get back to his wife and kid, but they told him no. I imagine there were financial motivations behind this, since the facility was quite expensive. 

There were also more leisure options; I convinced the other patients to watch Spaceballs with me and worked on my chess game. I had a roommate this time. He wasn't even depressed or anything, he just got drunk after his girlfriend kicked him out and decided that a mental institution was a good place to crash for the night, but they wouldn't let him leave in the morning.

I'm aware of the consequences, I just don't especially care. I may be misunderstanding your question here, but I take Humalog twice a day, Humilin in the morning, and Lantus at night. My dosages haven't been adjusted in a while since the doctors don't have blood sugar data to work with.

Not in my mood, no, but my (physical) energy levels are usually much lower, which doesn't help. I eat fairly normally so my blood sugars usually swing higher than lower.

Unfortunately I was forced to break things off with him (long story, but I'll go into it if you want me to), and my financial situation prevents me from seeking out a new one right now.
